raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60560.

The sliding-window KV manager frees blocks once they fall wholly outside a request's window, but the worker's persistent block table keeps the freed block ids. Attention kernels load KV in tiles (FA4 uses 128-key tiles on SM100). With 64-token pages, the tile that holds the window start can include one page lying wholly below the window. That page is masked, but masked NaN still propagates (0 × NaN). After the freed block is reused, its bytes can decode as NaN in the layer that reads it, and that request's attention output turns NaN.

#60560 has the full analysis. In short, on B300 with a DFlash2 drafter (all 6 layers sliding window, 2048) under the hybrid KV cache manager and `--block-size 64`:
- draft acceptance falls from about 40% to 27–29% at 32 concurrent sessions;
- the first divergence is NaN in the last draft layer's attention;
- about 21% of that layer's in-tile stale pages contain fp8 NaN bytes.

This PR makes the worker never hand those entries to attention. When `gather_block_tables` builds the forward-pass tables, every sliding-window entry wholly below `first_scheduled_position - (sliding_window - 1 + extra_retained_tokens)` is replaced by the null block:
- **No query of the step can attend those positions.**
- **The cutoff is never below the manager's free boundary.** The manager frees on the processed-token count, which is at most the first scheduled position, so every block it may have freed is covered.
- **Only the forward-pass copy changes.** Slot mappings and the persistent tables are untouched.
- **GPU only.** The first scheduled position is the request's `num_computed_tokens`, already on the device, so there is no host sync.
- **Every sliding-window spec is covered.** `SlidingWindowSpec.num_retained_tokens` gives the reach. (`KpoolTailSpec`, which an earlier revision opted out, was removed on `main` in #57169; its successor `CircularBufferSpec` is not a `SlidingWindowSpec` and is unaffected.)
- **Context parallelism is excluded.** Masking is disabled when `cp_size > 1`, where a block-table column is not a contiguous token range.

Speculator steps that reuse the gathered tables (e.g. DFlash) are covered too, since their queries sit at or after the target's first scheduled position.

### Scope

The change is not specific to any model or drafter. It applies to every KV cache group whose spec is a `SlidingWindowSpec` (including `SlidingWindowMLASpec`), target or draft, with any attention backend. Why it is safe:
- **No KV write is redirected.** Every KV write slot is computed from the persistent tables (`compute_slot_mappings`), or, for DFlash, from this step's positions, which are above the cutoff.
- **Entries are whole KV blocks.** Since #57169 `BlockTables` holds one entry per KV block, so the cutoff is `max(first_pos - reach, 0) // block_size` entries.

Not covered:
- **The V1 model runner.** The default V2 runner is covered; V1 is still selected for some speculators, DBO and some ROCm architectures.
- **Context parallelism (DCP/PCP).** Excluded on purpose, since a block-table column is not a contiguous token range there.
- **Chunked-local attention.** Not changed. Its chunk boundaries are multiples of the KV tile, so no wholly-outside page shares a tile.

**Assumption:** the null block holds no NaN. The KV cache is zero-allocated, and the null entries the tables already contain (sliding-window prefix hits, P/D tail clipping) rely on the same thing.

**Validation:** end-to-end validation so far covers a DFlash2 drafter under the hybrid KV cache manager. A check on a target model with sliding-window layers (e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 3) at high concurrency is still to do.

### Relation to existing PRs

- **#42276** (for #42273, "SWA eviction leaves stale block table entries") targets the same stale entries from the scheduler side: it resends the full rewritten block table to the worker after an eviction. It has had merge conflicts since May and no review. This PR is a worker-only alternative: no scheduler or `SchedulerOutput` change, and no table resend. If maintainers prefer #42276's direction, I'm happy to close this one in its favour, and the regression test here should carry over.
- **#53628** fixes the same NaN symptom inside the ROCm prefix-prefill kernel, by masking block-table loads. That is complementary kernel hardening; this PR keeps freed blocks out of every backend's tables.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`: the new `test_gather_block_tables_nulls_blocks_below_sliding_window` checks:
  - the exact cutoff, including a request with no scheduled tokens;
  - that full-attention groups are untouched;
  - padded rows;
  - that the persistent tables are left unchanged;
  - that rows are copied verbatim when no positions are passed.
- End-to-end on 2× B300, GLM-5.3 NVFP4 + DFlash2, prefill DEP8 / decode 2× TP4 over NIXL, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, `--block-size 64`, hybrid KV cache manager on, decode prefix caching off. Agentic multi-turn traffic (AgentX), 32 concurrent sessions, 900 s. Acceptance = accepted / drafted tokens over the profiling window.
- `pre-commit run ruff-check` and `pre-commit run mypy` on the changed files.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 11 passed on B300 (the new test and the 10 existing tests in the file).
- Rebased 2026-10-13 onto `main` `791f92135a` (#57169 removed `KpoolTailSpec` and kernel block sizes; the two review suggestions from @TheEpicDolphin are in): 16 passed, 0 failed on B300 (2026-10-14; `test_gpu_block_table.py` incl. the new test, plus the selected `test_kv_cache_utils` cases).
- ruff and mypy: passed.
- End-to-end, same build and traffic:

| | draft acceptance |
|---|---:|
| without this PR | 28.95% |
| **with this PR** | **41.21%** (819,107 / 1,987,756) |
| reference: hybrid KV cache manager off | 39.61% |

The end-to-end run used this exact diff on our serving build (vLLM 0.30.1-based), where it applies unchanged, because that stack (NVFP4 KV, NIXL whole-row registration) is not on `main` yet.

---

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate the bug and to draft this change and its test. I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

nodes.body: HiSparse added `block_table_updates`, which #42276 could use. The problem is it's quite expensive for SWA.

@TheEpicDolphin thanks for the review, all three addressed in 7a659e9e08.

- **KpoolTailSpec:** you're right. The tail ring is one block that every position maps into through `pos % block_size`, so the nulling would have hit its only entry once a request passed `2 * ring - 1` tokens, and the tail would stop being written. I added `SlidingWindowSpec.num_retained_tokens` (`sliding_window - 1 + extra_retained_tokens`) as you suggested, with `KpoolTailSpec` returning `None` to opt out; the runner maps `None` to a reach of 0, which the kernel already treats as disabled. `SlidingWindowMLASpec` keeps the base value, since it uses the same `SlidingWindowManager` and free boundary.
- **num_computed_tokens:** `seq_lens` is itself computed as `num_computed_tokens[req] + query_len`, so `seq_len - query_len` was always `num_computed_tokens[req]`. The kernel now reads that tensor directly by request slot, and the two batch-indexed arguments are gone. The test now places the requests in non-consecutive slots, so slot-vs-batch indexing is covered.
- **Load mask:** applied as written.

**Plumbline review** of #60767 at `51e63a1`.
Nothing blocking: one edge case in how a zero reach is treated, and two small cleanups.
Full report: https://plumbline-public-pr-852857244003-us-east-1-an.s3.amazonaws.com/0bfe75c2-b9e5-568a-a482-8f36beb21226/pull/60767/51e63a1cb15e8c0abdfd1c20a91c4b9da8c18f29/agent=deepseek~deepseek-v4.1-flash/judge=z-ai~glm-5.3/planner=xiaomi~mimo-v2.6-pro/2.html

1. **A reach of 0 doubles as "not a sliding-window group".** `sliding_window_reach` holds `num_retained_tokens` for sliding groups and 0 for the rest, and masking only happens when `reach > 0` (`block_table.py:59-63`, `319-321`). But `num_retained_tokens` is itself 0 when `sliding_window == 1` and `extra_retained_tokens == 0`, so that group gets no nulling while the manager still frees the blocks below its window (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1169-1172`). I don't know of a model with a 1-token window, so this is an edge case rather than a regression. A `-1` sentinel, or asserting the window is larger than 1, would close it.

2. **Docstring wording** (`kv_cache_interface.py:869-871`). "nulls a step's block-table entries wholly below that many tokens" reads as an absolute position, but the cutoff is `first_scheduled_position - num_retained_tokens`. Something like "more than that many tokens below the first scheduled position" would match the kernel.

3. **The new property could replace the copy right next to it.** `max_admission_blocks_per_request` still writes out `self.sliding_window - 1 + self.extra_retained_tokens` (`kv_cache_interface.py:895`), and `SlidingWindowManager.get_num_skipped_tokens` has the mirrored form. Using `num_retained_tokens` there keeps them from drifting.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I like the general approach, but it seems like `KpoolTailSpec`, which inherits from `SlidingWindowSpec`, would break from this change. It uses a one block ring buffer, and when `first_pos` gets large enough it will null that one block table entry.

Maybe we can add a `num_retained_tokens` method to both, and have it return None for `KpoolTailSpec` so that it opts out of the optimization? Just an idea.
`RequestStates` has a `num_computed_tokens` property that already contains the first token pos for each sequence. You may be able to pass that in instead of `query_start_loc` and `seq_lens` together.

files.patch:
@@ -307,6 +307,64 @@ def test_dummy_request_slot_mapping_is_pad():
     assert dummy[0].tolist() == [PAD_SLOT_ID] * 3
 
 
+def test_gather_block_tables_nulls_blocks_below_sliding_window():
+    """Entries wholly below the window of a request's first scheduled token
+    may point at blocks the sliding-window manager already freed and reused;
+    the forward-pass table must not hand them to attention."""
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    # Group 0 is full attention; group 1 is a 32-token sliding window
+    # (reach = sliding_window - 1 = 31).
+    block_tables = BlockTables(
+        block_sizes=[16, 16],
+        max_num_reqs=4,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=64,
+        max_num_blocks_per_group=[16, 16],
+        device=device,
+        sliding_window_reach=[0, 31],
+    )
+    full_ids = [list(range(1, 13)), list(range(41, 53))]
+    swa_ids = [list(range(21, 33)), list(range(61, 73))]
+    # Request slots 0 and 2: num_computed_tokens is indexed by slot, like the
+    # block tables, not by batch position.
+    req_slots = [0, 2]
+    for req, slot in enumerate(req_slots):
+        block_tables.append_block_ids(
+            req_index=slot,
+            new_block_ids=(full_ids[req], swa_ids[req]),
+            overwrite=True,
+        )
+    block_tables.apply_staged_writes()
+
+    idx_mapping = torch.tensor(req_slots, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    # Slot 0 has 145 computed tokens, so its first scheduled position is 145;
+    # slot 2 has 120.
+    num_computed_tokens = torch.tensor(
+        [145, 0, 120, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    )
+    full, swa = block_tables.gather_block_tables(
+        idx_mapping,
+        num_reqs_padded=3,
+        num_computed_tokens=num_computed_tokens,
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    assert full[0, :12].tolist() == full_ids[0]
+    assert full[1, :12].tolist() == full_ids[1]
+    # Request 0 reads back to 145 - 31 = 114: blocks 0..6 (tokens 0..111) are
+    # never read, block 7 (tokens 112..127) is.
+    assert swa[0, :12].tolist() == [0] * 7 + swa_ids[0][7:]
+    # Request 1 reads back to 120 - 31 = 89: blocks 0..4 are nulled.
+    assert swa[1, :12].tolist() == [0] * 5 + swa_ids[1][5:]
+    assert swa[2].count_nonzero().item() == 0
+    # Only the forward-pass copy changes.
+    assert block_tables.block_tables[1].gpu[0, :12].tolist() == swa_ids[0]
+
+    # Without num_computed_tokens the rows are copied verbatim.
+    _, swa = block_tables.gather_block_tables(idx_mapping, num_reqs_padded=2)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert swa[0, :12].tolist() == swa_ids[0]
+
+
 @pytest.fixture
 def populated_block_tables():

@TheEpicDolphin thanks for the review, all three addressed in 7a659e9e08.

- **KpoolTailSpec:** you're right. The tail ring is one block that every position maps into through `pos % block_size`, so the nulling would have hit its only entry once a request passed `2 * ring - 1` tokens, and the tail would stop being written. I added `SlidingWindowSpec.num_retained_tokens` (`sliding_window - 1 + extra_retained_tokens`) as you suggested, with `KpoolTailSpec` returning `None` to opt out; the runner maps `None` to a reach of 0, which the kernel already treats as disabled. `SlidingWindowMLASpec` keeps the base value, since it uses the same `SlidingWindowManager` and free boundary.
- **num_computed_tokens:** `seq_lens` is itself computed as `num_computed_tokens[req] + query_len`, so `seq_len - query_len` was always `num_computed_tokens[req]`. The kernel now reads that tensor directly by request slot, and the two batch-indexed arguments are gone. The test now places the requests in non-consecutive slots, so slot-vs-batch indexing is covered.
- **Load mask:** applied as written.

**Plumbline review** of #60767 at `51e63a1`.
Nothing blocking: one edge case in how a zero reach is treated, and two small cleanups.
Full report: https://plumbline-public-pr-852857244003-us-east-1-an.s3.amazonaws.com/0bfe75c2-b9e5-568a-a482-8f36beb21226/pull/60767/51e63a1cb15e8c0abdfd1c20a91c4b9da8c18f29/agent=deepseek~deepseek-v4.1-flash/judge=z-ai~glm-5.3/planner=xiaomi~mimo-v2.6-pro/2.html

1. **A reach of 0 doubles as "not a sliding-window group".** `sliding_window_reach` holds `num_retained_tokens` for sliding groups and 0 for the rest, and masking only happens when `reach > 0` (`block_table.py:59-63`, `319-321`). But `num_retained_tokens` is itself 0 when `sliding_window == 1` and `extra_retained_tokens == 0`, so that group gets no nulling while the manager still frees the blocks below its window (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1169-1172`). I don't know of a model with a 1-token window, so this is an edge case rather than a regression. A `-1` sentinel, or asserting the window is larger than 1, would close it.

2. **Docstring wording** (`kv_cache_interface.py:869-871`). "nulls a step's block-table entries wholly below that many tokens" reads as an absolute position, but the cutoff is `first_scheduled_position - num_retained_tokens`. Something like "more than that many tokens below the first scheduled position" would match the kernel.

3. **The new property could replace the copy right next to it.** `max_admission_blocks_per_request` still writes out `self.sliding_window - 1 + self.extra_retained_tokens` (`kv_cache_interface.py:895`), and `SlidingWindowManager.get_num_skipped_tokens` has the mirrored form. Using `num_retained_tokens` there keeps them from drifting.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I like the general approach, but it seems like `KpoolTailSpec`, which inherits from `SlidingWindowSpec`, would break from this change. It uses a one block ring buffer, and when `first_pos` gets large enough it will null that one block table entry.

Maybe we can add a `num_retained_tokens` method to both, and have it return None for `KpoolTailSpec` so that it opts out of the optimization? Just an idea.
Thanks for addressing the feedback, this looks good to me. I think it's a relatively safe short-term fix.
